title: Backblaze explains why it's sharing customer information with advertisers
gist: Backblaze's new privacy policy, effective December 1, discloses that since December 1, 2025 it has shared categories of account-level personal information (identifiers, commercial info, network activity, geolocation) with advertising and marketing partners, and that some may be 'sold or shared for targeted Advertising'. Backblaze says the disclosures cover website/marketing data, not encrypted backup file contents, and blames a confusing single-recipient table.

insights.claim: Backblaze's current privacy policy says it never rents, trades or shares customers' address or email with other companies for marketing without consent and makes no mention of advertisers.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Baseline for measuring how far the backup provider's data practices are moving toward ad monetization.
insights.quote: Under no circumstances do we rent, trade, or share your address or e-mail address with any other company for their marketing purposes without your consent.

insights.claim: Backblaze's new privacy policy, taking effect December 1, lists general personal information it says it has been collecting and sharing with third parties including advertising and marketing partners since December 1, 2025.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Retroactive disclosure of a year of ad-partner sharing may erode trust with privacy-sensitive backup customers.
insights.locator: On December 1, a new privacy policy takes effect

insights.claim: Under Backblaze's new policy, identifiers, commercial information, Internet or network activity and geolocation data may be sold or shared for targeted advertising, while sensitive data such as social security numbers, credit card numbers and precise geolocation is not shared with advertisers.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Shows even infrastructure/storage vendors are adding ad-data revenue streams — a churn risk if competitors market stronger privacy.

insights.claim: Backblaze says it updated its Privacy Notice to keep pace with a changing legal landscape that increasingly requires companies to spell out how they collect and use marketing-related information.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: State privacy laws are forcing more explicit 'sale/share' disclosures, surfacing previously quiet ad-tech practices across SaaS.
insights.quote: We updated our Privacy Notice to keep pace with the changing legal landscape
insights.locator: Renatta Siewert, Backblaze’s director of communications

insights.claim: Backblaze's upcoming privacy policy applies only to information collected about a customer's account, not to the content stored on its system, and Backblaze Computer Backup files are encrypted before being sent to the company.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: The core storage product's data remains outside ad sharing, limiting the commercial damage to account/marketing data.
insights.quote: only applies to the information collected in respect of your account and not to the content that you store on our system.

insights.claim: Backblaze says its sale and sharing disclosures relate to website and marketing data such as cookie-collected information and do not apply to files customers store with it, which it does not sell or share with advertisers, data brokers or analytics partners.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Company is drawing a firm line around stored data; any future breach of that line would be a major reputational event.
insights.locator: This is because the Privacy Notice’s sale and sharing

insights.claim: Backblaze says it does not sell or share sensory or surveillance data such as call recordings for targeted advertising, and attributes confusion to its policy table listing one set of recipients across all data categories, which its legal team will review.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Drafting ambiguity created a PR problem; watch whether the table is revised before or after the December 1 effective date.
insights.quote: The Privacy Policy table lists one set of recipients across all data categories, which is why it can read differently.
insights.locator: This has concerned some users, but a Backblaze spokesperson

insights.claim: Backblaze customers can opt out of the selling or sharing of their personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Opt-out (not opt-in) model means default monetization of account data.
insights.locator: Customers can use this link to opt out
